title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Note first that the neighbouring pages are not part of this manuscript. They are typescript pages 60–61 of SGA 7 Exposé IX (semistable reduction, Néron models, the M, M' lattices), interleaved in the scan. They have no mathematical relation to this page.

The page belongs to the 1976 IHÉS lecture notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. Grothendieck has a simplicial differential graded S-algebra A_* (he says 'semi-simpliciale', in the old sense of simplicial), with S = k{T} (braces denoting divided-power polynomial algebras). Its degree-n term A_n is a divided-power polynomial algebra in X_0,...,X_n, adjoined with differentials dX_i, modulo relations.
- Explicitly, A_1 = k{X_0,X_1}[dX_0,dX_1]/(dX_0 − dX_1).
- The relation dX_0 = dX_1 suggests the S-structure is given by something like T ↦ X_1 − X_0 (so that dT = 0). A Cartan–Sullivan-type 'forms on simplices' interpretation is another possibility. Both readings are hedged; the image does not settle it.
- A_0 = S, and the two face maps A_1 → A_0 are the two augmentations α, β.
- Functoriality is contravariant: a monotone σ: Δ_{n'} → Δ_n gives A_*(σ): A_n → A_{n'}.

Proposition. Let φ be an endomorphism of the differential S-algebra A_1 compatible with both augmentations α, β. Then for each n ≥ 0 there is a unique endomorphism φ_n of the differential S-algebra A_n such that φ_n ∘ A_*(σ) = A_*(σ) ∘ φ for every monotone σ: Δ_n → Δ_1. For n ≥ 1 it suffices to use a restricted family of such σ.

Corollary. φ_* = (φ_n) is an endomorphism of the simplicial differential S-algebra A_*, characterized by φ_1 = φ. Hence endomorphisms of A_* correspond bijectively, compatibly with composition, to the endomorphisms φ of the proposition.

Proof sketch for the corollary. One must check φ_{n'} A_*(σ) = A_*(σ) φ_n for every σ: Δ_{n'} → Δ_n.
- The case n = 0 is clear because A_0 = S.
- The case n = 1 is the hypothesis.
- For n ≥ 1, the images of A_1 under the maps A_*(τ) for τ: Δ_n → Δ_1 (surjective ones suffice) generate A_n as an algebra.
- So it suffices to check the identity after composing with these A_*(τ). That reduces to the defining property of φ_{n'} applied to the composite τσ: Δ_{n'} → Δ_1.

The point is that A_* is 'generated in simplicial degree 1'. Its endomorphism monoid is therefore computed by endomorphisms of A_1 over the two augmentations.

The left-margin notes ('2P_i = 0 ∀ i ≥ 1', '2φ^1(X_0^{(i)}) = 0', '2∂_i = 0') indicate a subsequent computation of these φ. It appears to show that the higher components of φ on divided powers X_0^{(i)} are 2-torsion. This is a step toward classifying all endomorphisms ('operations') of this PD de Rham model, presumably in connection with Frobenius- or Steenrod-type operations.
errors: Only the uniqueness and the 'generation' half of the argument are on the page. The existence of φ_n, i.e. that the prescribed values on generators respect the defining relations of A_n, is asserted, not proved here.
The phrase 'semi-simpliciale' is used while degeneracies (surjective σ) are invoked. This is old terminology for 'simplicial', not a mathematical error.

The draft is internally hesitant about which σ suffice (crossed-out and corrected parentheticals). The final version ('on peut se borner aux surjectifs') is correct, since monotone maps factor as a surjection followed by an injection.

ideas.what: Simplicial differential graded algebra of divided-power polynomial forms, used as an integral / char-p model for de Rham-type cochains
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial de Rham algebra (integral polynomial forms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: H. Cartan, 'Théories cohomologiques' (Invent. Math. 1976); Sullivan (rational case)

ideas.what: Endomorphisms of the simplicial dga A_* are determined by, and correspond bijectively to, endomorphisms of A_1 compatible with the two face maps, because A_n is generated by pullbacks of A_1 along maps Δ_n → Δ_1
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial object generated in degree 1 (1-coskeletal-type generation); determination of natural operations by the 1-simplex

ideas.what: Margin computation that the higher divided-power components of such endomorphisms are 2-torsion
ideas.modern_name: Classification of operations / endomorphisms of the PD de Rham model (Frobenius / Steenrod-type operations)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to classify all endomorphisms of the simplicial PD de Rham algebra A_* by reducing to degree 1. He begins computing them, with margin constraints like 2φ(X_0^{(i)}) = 0. A full computation of this endomorphism monoid, i.e. the 'natural operations' on the PD de Rham cochain model, does not seem to be a standard published result.
missed.quote: L'ens. des endom. de S-alg. diff. A_* est ainsi en correspondance biunivoque (conservant les compositions) avec l'ens. des φ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Operations on integral or mod-p cochain models (E_∞ / Steenrod structure, Frobenius lifts on PD algebras) are of current interest, e.g. in integral models for homotopy types and in de Rham–Witt and prismatic contexts. An explicit endomorphism monoid of the PD simplicial de Rham algebra would be a concrete datum. This is modest, since the reduction-to-degree-1 lemma itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma is a routine 'generated in degree 1' reduction. The context, a divided-power simplicial de Rham algebra and the classification of its endomorphisms with 2-torsion phenomena, is of some historical interest as an independent counterpart to Cartan's 1976 work. Little here is clearly new.
transcription_corrections: 'alors[?] qu'il existe' is likely 'Je dis qu'il existe' (or 'Alors il existe').
'telle que' should read 'tel que' (refers to endomorphism).
The neighbouring pages in the provided transcriptions are SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript pages (60–61), interleaved in the scan, not continuations of this manuscript.
'(ci-dessus[?] de la prop.)' is probably '(cf. énoncé de la prop.)' or '(comme dans la prop.)'.
In the proof: 'Alors on utilise que les A_*(σ)(A_1), σ: Δ_n → Δ_1 (on peut se borner aux surjectifs), sont des sous-algèbres/images qui engendrent l'algèbre A_n, donc il suffit de prouver que ...'.
The left-margin vertical notes read roughly: 'pour i ≥ 1 ... vu 2P_i = 0 ∀ i ≥ 1, i.e. 2φ^1(X_0^{(i)}) = 0 ∀ i ≥ 1 ... 2∂_i = 0'. They concern torsion constraints on the components of φ.
